title: Drawings, licence lists and grant rounds: one owner, more than one place
question: In each drawing or one-per-party list on disk, do entrants or winners belong to one owner-group, and who wins most often?
finding: Condominium lottery (2001 to 2013): 1,996 buildings made 6,987 entries and 818 wins; 7 building(s) show as a winner twice, and 2 registry owner(s) had a property business at two or more buildings entered in one drawing. Taxi medallions: 18 of 801 holder names hold more than one of the 1,145 medallions, the largest being SFFCU (San Francisco Federal Credit Union) Taxi Medallion Holder with 292. Cannabis: 17 owner-group(s) hold State licences under two or more legal names, and 60 more pairs share only an owner’s name. Grant rounds: 8 pair(s) of tied organizations were funded in the same round. Mobile food and street vending: 1 group(s) under two applicant names; 4 vending names appear twice.
how: Each file is tested for the same party appearing more than once: by name within the file, by owner-group (tiers 1 to 4) and by address lead (tiers 5 and 6). For the condominium lottery, which lists buildings and not owners, each building’s address is matched to registry owners that had a property business registered there in the lottery year; an owner counts only with two or more buildings in one drawing. Private individuals are shown as codes made from a hash; businesses and organizations are named. Rows on record evidence come first, then address matches, then name matches.
limits: The drawing results and published rules downloaded to the project's saved copy (not hosted here) are analysed separately (the site’s “Drawings and repeat winners” page), which also reads the owner-groups written here; this screen uses only the files named in its sources and quotes no rule, so which of these lists allows one entry per party should be checked before any row is read as a problem. A registry owner at a lottery building’s address may be a manager or a shop, not the applicant; the Assessor’s public roll does not name owners. The taxi and permit files show only current holders, with no history, and the same printed name can be two people. The two largest medallion holders are credit unions; the file does not say how they came to hold them. The City’s cannabis equity list, housing-lottery applicants and street-space drawings are not published. Surname-and-address matching (tier 6) could not be run on files that give no address.
